text: Griseofulvin acts as a repurposed inhibitor of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway, which is constitutively activated in Polycythemia Vera (PV) primarily due to the *JAK2* V617F mutation. Molecular docking studies suggest that Griseofulvin binds to the ATP-binding pocket of the JAK2 kinase domain, effectively competing with ATP and suppressing downstream phosphorylation of STAT3, thereby inhibiting the aberrant erythropoiesis characteristic of PV. While its binding affinity is in the micromolar range—lower than specialized JAK inhibitors like ruxolitinib—its established safety profile and ability to induce apoptosis in *JAK2*-mutated cells provide a rationale for its potential use in reducing the hematocrit and symptom burden in PV patients.
